title: Binary expansion of the quasi-polynomial budget
statement: For a finite bit string $x$, let $s$ be the concatenation of the all-true string obtained from the binary expansion of the length of $x$ after its first two bits are discarded, the bit $0$, and the all-true string obtained after discarding the first bit of that expansion. Define $Z(w)$ by scanning a bit string $w$ from left to right, outputting no bit until a zero has been encountered, and then outputting a zero for each subsequent input bit. Then the binary expansion of $2^{\lfloor\log_2 |x|\rfloor^2+1}$ is the concatenation of $Z$ applied to the strings obtained by successively discarding the first $i$ bits of $s$, for $i=0,1,\ldots,(|s|+1)+1-1$, followed by the two bits $0,1$.
